content:
Hi, I was pointed here from the mathlib stream.

I am looking for Lean 4 formalization infrastructure around first-order arithmetic and Gödel-style diagonalization.

More precisely, I would like to know whether Formalized Formal Logic exposes reusable components for:

  • syntax/coding of arithmetic formulas;
  • substitution;
  • proof coding or provability predicates;
  • a diagonal/fixed-point lemma;
  • Gödel's first incompleteness theorem or the machinery leading to it.

My goal is to build a small external Lean 4 file that imports this infrastructure and works with PA or a weak arithmetic theory.

Is FFL reasonably reusable as a library from another Lean 4 project, or is it mainly intended as a self-contained development/book?

Hello. One of the goals of FFL is to build a reusable, general-purpose library for logic. These results have been formalized in a reasonably general form.

  • Syntax and coding for formulas (If the term coding refers to the arithmetization of metamathematics, it has been formalized in Bootstrapping.)
  • Substitution. but it uses more abstract notion of rewriting because other systems (intuitionistic, second-order, ...) uses similar notion.
  • A provability predicate. There is also a more abstract treatment of provability predicates for provability logic.
  • A fixed-point lemma and its variations.
  • Gödel's first incompleteness theorem.

Moreover we have second incompleteness theorem and Solovay's arithmetical completeness theorem for GL\mathsf{GL}GL .

However, since this is an ongoing project, as with mathlib, there are often major changes to the foundational parts. Downstream projects should be aware that they may be affected by this. Additionally, compared to mathlib, the code may be less polished.
It should be noted that while we have Peano arithmetic, we have not shown that it is Δ1\Delta_1Δ1​-definable (not because it is difficult, but simply because it is too tedious).
